{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 represented PDB 1acc chain A, anthrax protective antigen, as one whole-chain domain: d1acca_ (SUNID 43828), classified in family f.11.1.1, superfamily f.11.1 and fold f.11, all named Anthrax protective antigen, within class f (Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides).

By SCOPe 2.05, this had been replaced by two domains; the same definitions persist in 2.06, 2.07 and 2.08:
• d1acca2 (SUNID 238522), A:14–225: PA14 family b.179.1.1, PA14-like superfamily b.179.1, Anthrax protective antigen N-terminal-like fold b.179, in class b (All beta proteins).
• d1acca1 (SUNID 238521), A:226–735: Anthrax protective antigen C-terminal-like family f.60.1.1, superfamily f.60.1 and fold f.60, in class f.
These ranges use PDB residue numbering; the SID suffixes do not indicate N-to-C sequence order.

This is a revision of the evolutionary units recognized within the same protein, not a biological change to the protein. Separating the N-terminal PA14 module exposes its evolutionary relationships independently of the remaining protective-antigen region. Domains can occur in different protein architectures and have distinct evolutionary histories. SCOPe evolutionary units also need not correspond one-for-one to every geometrically distinguishable structural subdomain. Family membership supports a closer relationship, while superfamily membership supports broader common ancestry; shared fold or class alone does not establish homology.

Homology searches should therefore use the two release-specific domain regions separately, alongside whole-chain searches when architecture matters. Domain-level sequence/profile and structural comparisons can detect PA14 relatives that lack the rest of protective antigen and avoid dilution of a local signal by unrelated sequence. Assess alignment coverage and domain architecture: a PA14-region hit supports a relationship for that region, not automatically for the entire chain or its C-terminal region. It does not justify transferring toxin function, exact biochemical activity, or the complete 1acc structure as a modeling template. Use templates over the supported homologous region, and record the SCOPe release and boundaries so that results based on the retired whole-chain definition are not treated as equivalent to the newer domain assignments.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of domain evolution and homology-search interpretation","mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1acc","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.75/sids/d1acca_","/api/v1/releases/1.75/sids/d1acca_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.05/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.06/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.07/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca2/parents"]}]}
